subject: Integration revenue-share: multi-tier commission mechanics and lead registration
messages:
From: Megan Liu <megan.liu@streamline.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: streamline-legal@streamline.ai
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on the rev-share tiers and lead registration flow

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the sync this morning — appreciate the clarity on the integration timeline. Two asks from our side so we can finalize the internal budget and cadence: 

1) Multi-tier mechanics: in the high-level doc you shared you showed 10% / 7% / 4% by ARR band. Can you confirm whether those percentages apply to gross platform revenue or to net revenue after Redwood credits/discounts? Also how do we treat usage credits bundled in co-marketing?

2) Lead registration: we need a durable lead registration window for inbound conversions (we typically insist on a 9–12 month protection window). Does Redwood support an MQL -> SQL handoff rule (timestamped) plus a lead ID we can reference when calculating commission?

If you can send a short redline or example calc, legal will review and we can loop in our finance team. Attaching our standard reseller checklist for your reference.

Thanks,

Megan Liu
Head of Partnerships | Streamline AI
megan.liu@streamline.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198
[Attachment: streamline_reseller_checklist.docx (DOCX)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Megan Liu <megan.liu@streamline.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on the rev-share tiers and lead registration flow

Megan — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, and I attached a short draft with examples.

- Percent base: percentages apply to gross platform invoice value before Redwood promotional credits. Co-marketing credits that we book as discounts are treated as contra-revenue for commission calculations (we exclude them).
- Lead registration window: Redwood supports a timebound registration ID (we can issue an ID at MQL capture) and a 12‑month protection window by default. We can shorten/extend in SOW.

I[0m've attached a draft rev-share schedule that shows two worked examples (a $50k ARR customer and a $300k ARR customer) to illustrate how commissions flow with discounts and crediting rules. Note the tier breakpoints are configurable before signature.

Next steps: can you confirm whether Streamline requires 1) payout on invoice vs settlement schedule and 2) clawback mechanics if a customer churns inside 90 days? Those two define how we model cashflow on our side.

Best,

Marcus Lin
Head of Partner Programs | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com
+1 (650) 555-0142
[Attachment: redwood_revshare_draft_v2.pdf (PDF), commission_calc_streamline.xlsx (XLSX)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Questions on the rev-share tiers and lead registration flow

Folks — forwarding Streamline's Qs and Marcus's draft. Quick context: Streamline is an ISV integration partner with a healthy pipeline; they want 12 months protection and prefer payout on invoice. Marcus flagged contra-revenue treatment for co-marketing credits (we exclude).

Inline from Marcus for reference:
> - Percent base: percentages apply to gross platform invoice value before Redwood promotional credits. Co-marketing credits that we book as discounts are treated as contra-revenue for commission calculations (we exclude them).
> - Lead registration window: Redwood supports a timebound registration ID (we can issue an ID at MQL capture) and a 12‑month protection window by default.

Questions for ops/legal: 
- Ben: can you confirm whether we can support payout on invoice (i.e., pay partner when invoice is issued to customer) vs our normal settlement schedule? Which systems/tracking IDs do we need?
- Karthik: commercial approval question — are the proposed bands (10%/7%/4%) acceptable for a first-phase deal and what guardrails should we ask (lead-sourced thresholds, self-sourced carveouts)?

If you can reply EOD Friday we'll push a revised SOW to Streamline legal.

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Director, Partner GTM | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Mar 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Questions on the rev-share tiers and lead registration flow

Marissa / Karthik — quick ops readout and attached calc. TL;DR: we can support payout on invoice but it requires 1) partner registration ID captured at MQL, 2) a matching field in our billing system, and 3) a short reconciliation lag (we push payment on next settlement run after invoice issuance). Suggested implementation: 

- Capture: Streamline includes partner_id param in signup / lead form -> our intake triggers a lead reg ticket in Salesforce with created_at timestamp and partner_id.
- Protection: 12 months from created_at (configurable). Track with lead_reg_id in accounting ledger.
- Payout timing: invoice-anchored payout; payments processed on the next payroll cycle (net 30 from invoice issue) to reduce friction.
- Clawbacks: apply if customer churns within 90 days; partner must repay net commission on next settlement. We propose a pro-rata clawback calculation (example in spreadsheet).

Attached: commission_calc_streamline.xlsx — includes three scenarios and a sample SQL query to pull the lead_reg_id / invoice matching. We recommend redline to SOW: 12-month protection, invoice-anchored payout (net 30), 90-day clawback.

Ben
VP, RevOps | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
[Attachment: commission_calc_streamline.xlsx (XLSX)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: streamline-legal@streamline.ai
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2027 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Integration revenue-share: multi-tier commission mechanics and lead registration

Team / Streamline legal — I reviewed the draft mechanics and Ben's scenarios. Approved to proceed with the following commercial guardrails for phase 1: 

- Tiers: 10% (0–100k ARR), 7% (100–500k ARR), 4% (500k+ ARR) applied to gross invoice value before Redwood promotional credits.
- Protection: 12-months by default from lead_reg created_at.
- Payout: invoice-anchored, processed net 30 on our settlement run.
- Clawback: 90-day churn pro-rata; partner refund obligation on next settlement run.
- Lead-sourced carveouts: partner must demonstrate lead ownership with timestamped lead_reg_id and initial qualifying activity (demo scheduled or SQL conversion).

Streamline legal: please prepare a short SOW redline reflecting the above and include an example commission schedule (we've attached the spreadsheet). Marcus — please share the revised SOW with Streamline and I'll sign off on commercial terms.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
